docNotes: ADR 0071 and runbook content-updates.md: until the alarm PR (#42's monitoring.ts) lands, no alarm reads these lines. Each refusal already logs its fixed line: CONTENT_NOT_LOADED (warn, 'pricing run found lines stopped by rule content not loaded for their dates', once per refused or complete run), WAITING_ON_CONTENT (warn, the monitor, once per plan), and RELEASE_READ_OUTSIDE_FETCH (error, 'pricing run read rule content outside the keys it fetched', once per failed run). The runbook should tell the operator to check the worker logs daily for these three error codes in that window.

Design 7.2 / the later PR's monitoring.ts row: add RELEASE_READ_OUTSIDE_FETCH (a worker log-group filter on error_code, paging the operator topic) beside CONTENT_NOT_LOADED and WAITING_ON_CONTENT. The design's string table must drop 'the operator was alerted' from release_read_outside_fetch and use the new text: '...which is PaidWhole's defect, so no line was kept and it was logged for the operator. The month is priced again by itself once it is fixed.'

Design 5.6.3 / ADR 0071: a month failed release_read_outside_fetch is planned again at each monitoring trigger, by intent (no wait), and fails at its first bad batch until the defect is fixed; it then prices by itself.

Design 5.6.5 / ADR 0071: a content-refused run whose other lines stopped on engine errors that page the operator also logs the PRICING_ENGINE_ERROR line, so 'the engine-error page stays' holds for refused runs too.

Design 5.6.5 content-alert table: no_gpci and no_conversion_factor under LOCKED:<year> terms are judged against the basis year (any window meeting that year), not the service date (M-1). Locality and plus-four keep the service date.
Design 5.6.7: TriageFacts.contentNotLoaded is required (no 'absent is false').

Design 5.8.6, runbook content-updates.md section 6 and test matrix RCC-08: the Releases card lists each dated family of the release in force in one of these forms: '<title>: loaded through <date>', '<title>: in force, no end date', '<title>: loaded only from <date>' (or 'from a later date'), '<title>: only partly loaded in this release' (some but not every content has records), '<title>: not loaded in this release'.

Design / ADR 0071 (content-through cache): Coverage reads only pfs_rvu windows and Releases only the dated families' record types; the console reads every content. The cache is keyed by release, manifest and record-type set.

Design 5.6.2 precedence (int-money improvement 3): when a run hits both a location stop and a content gap, the customer's location step is shown first. The content wait is learned only on the next run, and no CONTENT_NOT_LOADED line is logged for a location-refused run, even when every line also read content outside its span.
Later PR (int-money improvement 2): consider NCCI PTP as a fourth span content, or a triage hold. A PTP quarter that is not loaded drops NCCI_REVIEW holds without notice.

dispositions.what: Step 23 found a real defect that predates this PR. A triage of practice A's 100,000-line period fails with Postgres 53200 'out of shared memory' (hint: max_locks_per_transaction). So does A's audit report, which runs triage inline (generate.ts:73). The cause: line_status_rules() takes pg_advisory_xact_lock per inserted line_status row (migrations 20261019160000, 20261022090000, 20261023120000). advanceStages (apps/worker/src/triage/execute.ts:330) inserts about 60,000 lines in one transaction, which overflows the lock table (64 x connections). B's 12,170 lines pass. The Docker runtime (max_connections=200) and RDS defaults are also below 60,000, so production would fail too. The best fix is a migration (one lock per statement or per practice in the trigger) or an RDS parameter-group change (max_locks_per_transaction, mirrored in the harness's Postgres). Both are outside this round's hard rules: no migration, nothing under packages/db, and the trigger is the ledger's existing behaviour. Splitting triage into several transactions would change triage's atomicity, which is out of proportion for a suite fix. Hand it to Lane A.

docNotes: ADR 0071 / design 5.10 and runbook content-updates or screening-capacity: the first full-size release-capacity run (process runtime, 2026-10-26) fails on A's triage and A's audit report. The cause is the per-line pg_advisory_xact_lock in line_status_rules(), which overflows the lock table on about 60,000 lines in one transaction. This is a release-1 sizing blocker for Lane A: change the trigger in a migration or raise max_locks_per_transaction in the RDS parameter group, and set the same value in the harness's Postgres (tools/screening-capacity/containers.ts passes only shared_buffers and max_connections).

docs/runbooks/screening-capacity.md 'Running it elsewhere' (process runtime): the worker process does not inherit PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, so Playwright looks in ~/.cache/ms-playwright. On a machine whose browsers are elsewhere (here /opt/pw-browsers), audit_report fails until that path holds chromium_headless_shell at the pinned revision (1194). The runbook should say so, or ProcessRuntime should pass the variable through.

Design 5.10: the windows query measured 12,848 ms and 10,125 ms cold, against its 5,000 ms advisory budget, on an unlimited local Postgres 18. The plan is a GroupAggregate over all 4.17M rule_record rows with about 557k temp blocks read. It is advisory, but it is worth an index or a summary table in the later PR.
